title: RevOps process: Marketplace deal ops in HubSpot (AWS + GCP)
content:
Audience
- AEs/AMs selling Redwood through AWS Marketplace or GCP Marketplace
- SEs supporting procurement/onboarding
- Deal Desk / RevOps / Finance for approvals + reconciliation

Purpose
Standardize how we create + track marketplace-sourced deals in HubSpot so that:
- Forecasting reflects marketplace timing (subscription/offer acceptance vs first usage)
- Provisioning + entitlement handoffs are not dropped
- Finance can reconcile marketplace payout/invoices to the correct account + SKU/term
- CS sees the right onboarding motion (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Scope (what this doc covers)
- HubSpot objects to use (Deal + Company + Contacts) and required properties
- Deal stages + forecasting rules for marketplace transactions
- Handoffs: AE/SE -> Solutions/Onboarding -> CS/Support -> Finance
- Private offer process (AWS/GCP) and approvals
- Edge cases (existing org, multiple subscriptions, entitlement delays)

Not in scope
- Pricing guidance / discount policy (see AWS private offer template notes + CRO approvals thread)
- Detailed security questionnaire answers (see security packet + questionnaire draft)

Definitions (quick)
- Marketplace Subscription: customer clicks “Subscribe” (public offer) in AWS/GCP marketplace.
- Private Offer: custom terms presented via AWS/GCP marketplace; customer accepts in marketplace console.
- Entitlement: marketplace signal that the customer is authorized for Redwood service/SKU; used for org provisioning and limits.
- Redwood Org: tenant in Redwood Console; can be linked to marketplace subscription(s).


1) When to use a “Marketplace Deal” in HubSpot
Create a HubSpot Deal when ANY of the following is true:
- Procurement requires marketplace purchase (even if opportunity originated elsewhere)
- Customer is accepting a private offer through AWS/GCP
- We need to forecast a capacity reservation/annual commit that will be transacted via marketplace

Do NOT create a Marketplace Deal for:
- Pure PLG self-serve usage on Redwood website with standard card billing
- Exploratory conversations where marketplace is “maybe” and there is no procurement action yet (log as an activity, create deal once marketplace path is confirmed)


2) HubSpot: Deal naming convention
Deal Name format (required)
- {Account Name} – {AWS|GCP} Marketplace – {Hosted|Dedicated|Private} – {YYYY-Q#}
Examples
- Northpeak Analytics – AWS Marketplace – Hosted – 2026-Q1
- Europa Insurance – GCP Marketplace – Private – 2026-Q2

Why: keeps pipeline views clean and avoids duplicates when the same account has both direct and marketplace motions.


3) Required HubSpot properties (Deal)
All Marketplace Deals MUST have these fields completed within 24 hours of deal creation.

Deal basics
- Deal owner (AE) (required)
- SE owner (required once SE engaged)
- Deal type (picklist): New Business | Expansion | Renewal
- Procurement route (picklist): AWS Marketplace | GCP Marketplace
- Marketplace offer type (picklist): Public Offer | Private Offer
- Marketplace product (picklist): Hosted API | Dedicated | Private
- Primary SKU / Package (picklist): use “Marketplace SKU Catalog v2” naming (Hosted-Base, Hosted-Scale, Dedicated-Reservation, Private-Platform, Compliance-Add-on, etc.)
- Term (picklist): Monthly | Annual | Multi-year
- Close date (required)
- Amount (required): commit value / contract value used for forecasting (see section 6)

Marketplace identifiers (required when known)
- AWS Marketplace Customer Identifier (string) OR GCP Billing Account ID (string)
- Marketplace Subscription ID / Entitlement ID (string)
- Private offer ID (string) (only for private offers)
- Offer acceptance date (date) (private offer)

Provisioning / onboarding
- Redwood Org status (picklist): Not created | Created (unlinked) | Linked to subscription | Active usage observed
- Redwood Org ID (string)
- Desired region / residency (string) (if relevant; especially EMEA + regulated)
- Target go-live date (date)
- Support tier (picklist): Standard | Premium SLA | Private (Enterprise)

Attribution
- Lead source (standard)
- Marketplace origin (picklist): AWS listing | GCP listing | AE-sourced | Partner referral | Customer requested
- Marketplace listing SKU selected (string) (what they clicked/subscribed to; useful for conversion analysis)

Data quality note
- If an ID is not yet known, set a task “Fill marketplace identifiers” due within 7 days, and update once the subscription/offer is accepted.


4) Required HubSpot properties (Company)
For marketplace reconciliation, ensure the Company record includes:
- Cloud preference (picklist): AWS | GCP | Multi
- Primary cloud account (free text): AWS account alias OR GCP project/billing account nickname used by the buyer
- Industry (standard)
- Security/compliance notes (free text) (high-level only; detailed evidence stays in security packet)


5) Deal stages (Marketplace pipeline)
We use the standard Enterprise pipeline stages, with marketplace-specific definitions.

Stage definitions + required exit criteria
1. Qualified
- Marketplace route confirmed OR procurement team requested marketplace purchase.
- Required fields: Procurement route, Marketplace product.

2. Solutioning / Discovery
- SKU fit confirmed (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- If Dedicated/Private: requirements captured (SLOs, regions, security).
- Required fields: Primary SKU, Term.

3. Marketplace Offer In Progress
Public offer path:
- Customer is preparing to subscribe OR has subscribed and is awaiting entitlement/provisioning.
Private offer path:
- Offer terms drafted; approval process started.
- Required fields: Marketplace offer type, Amount, Close date.

4. Offer Sent / Subscription Initiated
Public offer:
- Subscription created in AWS/GCP console (customer indicates they subscribed).
Private offer:
- Offer sent via marketplace tooling (offer ID if available).
- Required fields: Marketplace subscription/entitlement ID OR private offer ID (as soon as available).

5. Closed Won (Marketplace)
Set to Closed Won when:
- Private offer accepted in marketplace OR public subscription completed AND entitlement confirmed.
- For Dedicated/Private, if there is a gating dependency (e.g., SOW for on-prem), log that in notes but do not delay Closed Won if marketplace acceptance is complete.
- Required fields: Offer acceptance date (private offers) OR subscription/entitlement ID (public), Redwood Org status at least “Created”.

6. Closed Lost
Use standard reasons + add “Marketplace” context in notes:
- Lost – Chose competitor (marketplace)
- Lost – Procurement stalled / no marketplace approval
- Lost – Security requirements unmet


6) Forecasting + amount rules (IMPORTANT)
Marketplace timing can differ from usage; forecast should reflect when the customer commits in the marketplace.

Which number goes into Deal Amount?
- Hosted (usage-based): use expected first-12-month spend (AE best estimate) if the buyer is making an annual commit via marketplace; otherwise use $0 and rely on usage dashboards (note in deal). If customer is required to buy through marketplace but there is no commit, keep Amount at $0 and track via “Expected monthly usage” note.
- Dedicated: use reservation/commit value (monthly or annual) that will be billed via marketplace.
- Private: use platform fee + support tier value that will be billed via marketplace.
- Add-ons (compliance/retention): include only if explicitly in the offer.

Forecast category guidance
- Pipeline: stages 1–2
- Best Case: stage 3 when internal approvals pending but customer intent is strong
- Commit: stage 4 when subscription initiated or private offer is out and buyer confirms internal approval is in-flight
- Closed Won: stage 5 after acceptance/subscription + entitlement confirmation

Close date guidance
- Close date should reflect marketplace acceptance date target (not “first API call”).
- If entitlement propagation is delayed after subscription, do NOT push the close date automatically; track provisioning issues via onboarding tasks (see section 7) and flag Support if >24 hours.


7) Handoffs + task checklist
A) AE -> SE (solutioning)
Trigger: customer requests Dedicated/Private, private offer, or has security/procurement blockers.
- Create/confirm SE owner on deal
- Attach notes: product chosen, target region, expected volumes/latency requirements
- Link any security questionnaire request and planned review call

B) AE/SE -> Provisioning / Onboarding (post-subscription)
Trigger: public subscription confirmed OR private offer accepted.
Create tasks (or use the “Marketplace onboarding” task template):
- Verify entitlement (AWS/GCP) in Redwood console tooling
- Create Redwood Org (if not existing)
- Link subscription to Org
- Confirm SKU limits/quotas applied correctly
- Send “First API key” instructions and marketplace onboarding docs link

SLA
- Entitlement verification attempt within 4 business hours of customer confirmation (same day where possible)
- Escalate to Support if entitlement not visible within 24 hours

C) Onboarding -> CS (ongoing)
Trigger: first successful request OR Dedicated/Private environment provisioned.
- Update Redwood Org status to “Active usage observed”
- Assign CSM (if applicable) and note support tier
- If Dedicated/Private: record launch date + owners

D) AE/RevOps -> Finance (reconciliation)
Trigger: Closed Won.
- Ensure marketplace identifiers present (customer ID/billing acct + entitlement/subscription)
- Confirm Amount and Term
- Add note: “Marketplace txn—expect payout/invoice via {AWS|GCP}”


8) Private offers: approvals + notes
AWS/GCP Private Offer requires approvals BEFORE sending to customer.
Minimum approvals (internal)
- CRO (Jordan Blake) for non-standard discounting or multi-year structures
- Finance sponsor (Laura Bennett) for revrec implications if structure is atypical
- Legal sponsor (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes) for any non-standard terms

HubSpot fields to complete for private offer deals
- Marketplace offer type = Private Offer
- Private offer ID (once created)
- Offer acceptance date (once accepted)
- Attach approval artifacts (email thread link or Slack timestamp) in deal notes


9) Common edge cases (how to log + what to do)
1) Customer already has a Redwood Org (existing direct user) and now procurement mandates marketplace
- Keep the same Company record
- Create a new Marketplace Deal (don’t overwrite the direct billing deal)
- Set Redwood Org status: “Created (unlinked)” then “Linked to subscription”
- Ensure “Marketplace origin” is set to “Customer requested”

2) Multiple marketplace subscriptions (same company, different teams)
- Prefer one Company, multiple Deals (one per subscription/commit) OR one Deal with “Multi-subscription” note if procurement bundles.
- Always capture each Subscription/Entitlement ID in notes (and in fields where supported).

3) Entitlement propagation delay
Symptoms: customer subscribed, but Redwood cannot validate entitlement yet.
- Set task “Retry entitlement verification” with timestamp
- If >24 hours: open Support ticket and reference known incident pattern (see SUP-4821)
- Communicate to customer: expected timing window + we’ll confirm when active

4) Billing dimension mismatch / SKU confusion
- Log in deal notes what SKU customer believed they purchased
- Escalate to Billing/Eng and reference SUP-4829 if similar
- Do not mark Closed Won until entitlement reflects correct SKU OR Finance confirms workaround is acceptable


10) Reporting (where to look)
Standard HubSpot views (RevOps maintained)
- Marketplace Pipeline (AWS vs GCP)
- Deals missing required marketplace fields (data hygiene)
- Closed Won marketplace deals pending Org link (handoff risk)

KPIs we are tracking for the listing refresh
- Marketplace lead -> subscription conversion rate
- Median time: subscription -> entitlement verified -> org linked -> first successful request
- % deals with complete identifiers at Closed Won (reconciliation readiness)

Instrumentation note
- Engineering is adding funnel telemetry (ENG-22114 / PR-19877). HubSpot is still source of truth for commercial state.


11) Contacts / escalation
RevOps (process + HubSpot fields): Isabelle Laurent
Marketplace GTM sponsor: Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineering escalation: Markus Klein
Support escalation owner (provisioning delays): Dev Patel
Security packet / evidence routing: Olga Petrov / Naomi Feldman


Appendix A: Quick checklist (copy/paste)
For any Marketplace Deal:
- Deal name uses convention
- Procurement route + offer type set
- Marketplace product + primary SKU set
- Amount + close date set (per rules)
- Marketplace identifiers added when known (customer ID, subscription/entitlement, offer ID)
- Redwood Org status tracked and updated
- Post-subscription tasks created (verify entitlement, link org, first API key)

Open questions (RevOps)
- For Hosted usage-only marketplace subscriptions with no commit: do we standardize on Amount = $0 vs estimated 12-month usage? (proposal: Amount=$0, track estimate in notes + a dedicated property)
- Do we need separate pipeline stages for “Entitlement confirmed” vs “Org linked” for operational clarity? (Ben + Chloe reviewing onboarding flow impacts)
